frequency_question: How often do major comprehensive energy/permitting reform bills clear all structural friction points and become law within a specified multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major legislative packages explicitly focused on energy permitting, NEPA reform, or interstate transmission/pipeline streamlining that advanced to serious floor consideration or major bipartisan compromise negotiations; excludes minor single-issue riders or non-energy infrastructure bills.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007

coverage_note: 4 major attempts identified; captures the primary bipartisan structural reform cycles of the modern era.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller rider provisions attached opportunistically to must-pass appropriations bills.
skeleton: Comprehensive energy permitting reform attempts: 4 major legislative pushes over 20 years, yielding 2 major enactments of broader energy packages (though comprehensive standalone permitting reform specifically failed multiple times).
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 major structural attempts
validity_reason: The structural polarization and Senate filibuster rules governing energy and environmental policy are stable baseline features of the US legislative process likely to persist through the decade.
